verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The equality itself is stated verbatim: A (x, φ) = a x ∧ C (x, φ) = a x * m x is (a_L, -b_L) = (a, -b_s) under the same dictionary as (C.1) (Lean's C is -b_L, a*m is -b_s), for every loop angle φ. Two differences in how the collar is described. (i) Lean measures the collar to the compact set B rather than to ∂I: the conclusion holds for x ∈ K with dist(x, B) < δ. B is the set on which the paper's extra hypothesis v_s > 2 is assumed (Lean's htrueB : ∀ x ∈ B, 2 < nominalSpeed (a x) (m x)), which the paper assumes 'in neighborhoods of both radial endpoints'; taking E = ℝ², K = I × [-1,1] and B = ∂I × [-1,1] (allowed, and named in the docstring of exists_compact_trueCone_family at TrueConeLoop.lean:728-731 as 'the two interval boundary faces'), dist((X,η), B) < δ holds whenever dist(X, ∂I) < δ, so the Lean conclusion with δ_∂ := δ gives exactly (C.3), η ∈ [-1,1] and φ included. (ii) Packaging: the paper gives δ_∂ inside the statement of Lemma C.1, while in Lean the agreement clause is part of exists_local_family_with_margin (as an open neighborhood N of B) and the positive uniform width δ is extracted by the separate theorem uniform_boundary_collar in the same file, whose hypothesis is exactly that clause. Conjoining the two is immediate.
